bound: No mechanism available to this work package removes the cost of the host being unavailable or of nobody being signed in. The measured window lost 24 triggers to an absent session; the only two mechanisms that would have scheduled through it are an S4U task (needs the batch-logon right) and automatic logon (needs a stored password). Everything else recovers minutes around the edges.

AUTOMATIC_LOGON.detail: automatic logon re-creates the session after a reboot and requires the account password to be stored on the machine; this work package holds no credential and will not acquire one

S4U_TASK.detail: S4U runs whether or not a session exists and stores no credential; it needs the 'log on as a batch job' right, which this process cannot grant itself
S4U_TASK.operator_command: schtasks /create /tn "<task>" /xml <definition with LogonType=S4U> /f — registered by an administrator, after granting the batch-logon right

recommendation.not_applied: the live task is left exactly as WP-EDGE-04 registered it: re-registering a running lane's task changes the phase the audit measures and is a deployment decision for the operator, not a side effect of an audit
recommendation.what_s4u_would_buy: the session dependence disappears: the 24 triggers lost to NO_SESSION would be scheduleable. It is blocked on the batch-logon right, so it needs an operator with administrator rights.
recommendation.what_the_logon_trigger_buys: it bounds the recovery from a sign-in to the trigger delay; the absence itself is untouched, so it recovers minutes, not the hours the absence consumed
recommendation.what_the_witness_buys: the 1 trigger(s) that end as SILENT_UNATTRIBUTABLE would become attributable, without needing the Task Scheduler's operational log
